subject: Daniel
note: Evidence for Daniel's Bible figure page. Every quotation is in daniel.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/daniel/ (gitignored): the BSB chapters quoted (bsb-daniel-chapters.txt, one verse a line; bsb-daniel-running.txt, the same chapters as running text for quotations that cross verses), the World English Bible's Greek Daniel (chapters 1, 3, 6, 13, 14) and 1 Maccabees 2 (web-daniel-greek.txt and -running.txt, copied from shared/), Josephus (Whiston, Gutenberg 2848, copied from people/moses/), the Catholic Encyclopedia (Daniel; Book of Daniel; Hippolytus), the 1911 Britannica (Daniel, with Daniel, Book of, and Susanna), Jerome's Commentary on Daniel (Archer 1958, tertullian.org, marked public domain by Roger Pearse), Origen's Letter to Africanus (newadvent), Benjamin of Tudela (Adler 1907, Gutenberg 14981), the BCP Morning Prayer (Church of England), the OCA (17 December list and life), azbyka.ru (30 December), the Greek synaxarion (17 December) and the Coptic synaxarium (23 Baramhat). Clement, Ambrose, Cyril and the 1916 Martyrology are the copies in shared/.

life.text: In the third year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem. Ashpenaz brought in young men 'from the royal family and the nobility', to learn the language and literature of the Chaldeans for three years. Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah were renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.

Daniel would not defile himself with the king's food or wine; ten days of vegetables and water; they looked healthier; the king found them ten times better than all the magicians. Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.

Carried captive 'When still a youth, probably about fourteen years of age', in the fourth year of Joakim (605 BC). At the writing on the wall 'The prophet, now at least eighty years of age'. Daniel means 'God is my judge'. Baltassar is read as Balatsu-usur, 'Bel protect his life'. Jewish tradition, 'accepted by many Fathers of the Church', held he was made a eunuch; 'this does not necessarily follow'. Jewish traditions say the king had sent him away before the furnace. Benjamin of Tudela was shown his tomb at Susa in 1165; the Roman Martyrology keeps him on 21 July.
life.note: Daniel 1:1 says the third year of Jehoiakim; the CE writes the fourth (Jeremiah's reckoning). The page gives the Bible's wording and the CE's date.

life.text: Josephus: four of the family of Zedekiah, Daniel, Ananias, Misael and Azarias, renamed Baltasar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. Daniel built a tower at Ecbatana where the kings of Media, Persia and Parthia were buried, kept by a Jewish priest 'to this day'. He was 'one of the greatest of the prophets'; 'he also determined the time of their accomplishment'. When Alexander was shown the book of Daniel, 'he supposed that himself was the person intended'.
life.note: The tower is not on the page any more (cut to fit the numbers column).

life.text: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue: the wise men could not tell it; the decree to kill them; Daniel asked for time; his friends pleaded; revealed in a vision of the night; Daniel's blessing (2:20-23); 'there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries'; the king fell on his face; ruler over the province of Babylon.
life.source: Daniel 2 (BSB). Daniel 2:4: the astrologers answered 'in Aramaic'.

life.text: The furnace: the golden statue; the three would not bow; 'But even if He does not'; seven times hotter; the fourth man 'like a son of the gods'; 'Not a hair of their heads was singed'. Daniel is not named in the chapter.
life.note: The Greek Daniel adds the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three (Daniel 3:24-90 in Catholic Bibles; WEB DAG 3).

life.text: Nebuchadnezzar's letter: the tree cut down; Daniel alarmed; 'may the dream apply to those who hate you'; his counsel (4:27); twelve months later the boast on the roof; driven out, ate grass like an ox; sanity restored; he praised the King of heaven.

Belshazzar's feast: the temple vessels; the hand; the queen; Daniel refused the gifts but read MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN; 'That very night Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans was slain'; Darius the Mede received the kingdom at sixty-two.

Darius: 120 satraps and three administrators including Daniel; no charge found 'unless ... concerning the law of his God'; the thirty-day decree; windows open toward Jerusalem, three times a day; the den sealed; the night of fasting; 'My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions'; no wounds 'because he had trusted in his God'; the decree to fear the God of Daniel; he prospered under Darius and Cyrus.

The visions: four beasts, the Ancient of Days, One like the Son of Man (7); the ram and the goat, Gabriel named (8:16); Jeremiah's seventy years, the prayer, Gabriel 'about the time of the evening sacrifice', 'you are highly precious', seventy weeks (9); three weeks of mourning without meat or wine, the man in linen by the Tigris, the prince of Persia twenty-one days, Michael (10); the last words, 'go on your way until the end' (12:13).
life.source: Daniel 7 to 12 (BSB). Mark 14:61-63 for Jesus' answer at His trial in the words of Daniel 7:13.

life.text: Susanna: Joakim's wife; the two elders; 'It is better for me to fall into your hands'; condemned; God raised up 'the holy spirit of a young youth, whose name was Daniel'; 'Are you all such fools'; examined apart: a mastic tree, an evergreen oak; convicted by their own words.
life.source: Susanna, DAG 13 in the World English Bible British Edition (Catholic Daniel 13).
life.note: The WEB renders both punishments 'cut you in two'; the Greek puns (schinos/schisei, prinos/prisei) are from the 1911 Britannica's Susanna article and Origen.

life.text: Bel and the Dragon: at the court of Cyrus; Bel's daily twelve measures of flour, forty sheep, six firkins of wine; Daniel laughed; the ashes; the footprints; seventy priests with wives and children; the dragon burst with pitch, fat and hair; 'The king has become a Jew'; six days with seven lions; Habakkuk carried 'by the hair of his head'; 'You have remembered me, O God!'; the king found him sitting on the seventh day.
life.source: Bel and the Dragon, DAG 14 in the World English Bible British Edition (Catholic Daniel 14).

life.text: Mattathias dying: 'Daniel was delivered from the mouth of lions for his innocence.'

Ezekiel names Daniel with Noah and Job (14:14, 20) and 'you are wiser than Daniel' (28:3). The CE takes this as our Daniel; the 1911 Britannica argues 'this could not be our Daniel' but an older celebrated figure.
life.source: Ezekiel 14:14, 20; 28:3 (BSB); Catholic Encyclopedia, Daniel; 1911 Britannica, Daniel.

dating.text: Porphyry's twelfth book denied the book was written by Daniel, 'but rather by some individual living in Judaea at the time of the Antiochus who was surnamed Epiphanes'. Jerome: 'this very attack testifies to Daniel's accuracy'; 'none of the prophets has so clearly spoken concerning Christ as has this prophet Daniel'.
dating.source: Jerome, Commentary on Daniel, prologue, tr. Gleason L. Archer (1958), transcribed by Roger Pearse: 'All material on this page is in the public domain'.
dating.note: A page mark '|16' interrupts the second quotation in the transcription; the evidence entry uses two parts.

dating.text: Traditional view: 'The traditional view, in vigour chiefly among Catholics' refers the book to Daniel (570-536 BC); testimonies Matthew 24:15, Josephus on Alexander, 1 Maccabees; 'Christian tradition ... practically unanimous'. The rival theory 'widely accepted by contemporary scholars' refers it to Antiochus IV; critics cite late Hebrew, Persian words and 'at least three Greek words'. Deuterocanonical parts: in the Septuagint, Theodotion and Vulgate; 'In the Hebrew Bible, and in most recent Protestant versions' the book is limited to the protocanonical parts; Trent decreed them canonical.
dating.source: Catholic Encyclopedia (1908), Book of Daniel, F. Gigot.

dating.text: The 1911 Britannica (J. D. Prince and R. H. Charles): the book 'now generally regarded as a production dating from the time of Antiochus Epiphanes (175-164 B.C.)'; the predictions 'become inaccurate as soon as the author finishes the section describing the reign of Antiochus'; Jesus' allusion 'shows merely that our Lord was referring to the work by its commonly accepted title'; 'The Book of Daniel loses none of its beauty and force...'. The book 'stands between Ezra and Esther' in the Hagiographa; Hebrew in 1-2:4 and 8-12, Aramaic 2:4-7; Gabriel and Michael 'are even mentioned by name'; traditions of burial in the royal vault at Babylon, of a return to Jerusalem (the rabbis), and Benjamin of Tudela's tomb at Susa.
dating.note: Britannica online could not be fetched (error pages); 'Most modern scholars' rests on the 1908 and 1911 encyclopedias, which already called it the prevailing critical view.

fathers.text: 1 Clement 45: 'Was Daniel cast into the den of lions by such as feared God? ...'
Ambrose: 'How unconquerable was Daniel, who feared not the lions raging round about him. The beasts roared, whilst he was eating.'
fathers.source: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy, book 1, chapter 35 (shared/npnf210.txt).
fathers.note: The heading above the line in npnf210 is Chapter XXXV of Book I.

fathers.text: Cyril of Jerusalem: Nebuchadnezzar rightly said the Holy Spirit was in Daniel, 'but he was not the master of the magicians, for he was no magician, but was wise through the Holy Ghost.'
fathers.source: Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lecture 16, chapter 31 (shared/npnf207.txt).

fathers.text: Origen answers Africanus on Susanna: 'the play of words between prinos and prisis, schinos and schisis. You say that you can see how this can be in Greek, but that in Hebrew the words are altogether distinct. On this point, however, I am still in doubt'.
fathers.source: Origen, Letter to Africanus, chapter 6 (ANF 4, tr. Crombie), at newadvent.

later.text: Benjamin of Tudela at Susa: the sepulchre of Daniel before a synagogue; the two sides of the river quarrelled and took the coffin a year each; Sinjar Shah-ben-Shah had it put in a coffin of crystal hung from the middle of the bridge by an iron chain; 'And to this very day the coffin is suspended from the bridge.' Adler's note: the reputed sepulchre lies near the mound of Susa.
later.source: The Itinerary of Benjamin of Tudela, tr. Marcus Nathan Adler (1907), Gutenberg 14981.
later.note: The CE dates the visit to 1165.

later.text: Coptic synaxarium, 23 Baramhat: the departure of the great prophet Daniel, 'in the last year of king Cyrus'; he 'remained in Babylon for seventy years, then departed in peace.'
later.note: 23 Baramhat is 1 April: Paremhat begins on 10 March (shared/wikipedia-coptic-calendar.txt).

later.text: OCA: Daniel and his three friends 'all survived into old age, but died in captivity'; they are also commemorated on the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers (the Sunday before the Nativity).

feasts.text: 21 July: 'At Babylon, the holy prophet Daniel.'
feasts.note: The present Roman Martyrology (2004) was not fetched.

feasts.text: 17 December: Daniel the Prophet and the Three Young Men, Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod.
feasts.note: Not in the Church of England (shared/cofe-calendar.txt), the Episcopal Church (shared/lff2022.txt) or the ELCA list.

feasts.text: 17 December: the Prophet Daniel and the three holy youths Ananias, Azarias and Misael, OCA and Greek synaxarion; 30 December (civil) in the Russian Church, with the troparion 'Велики веры свершения!' (translated on the page as ours).
feasts.source: OCA 17 December list; synaxarion.gr 17 December; azbyka.ru 2026-12-30.

feasts.text: The Benedicite ('O all ye Works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord') is set at Morning Prayer in the Book of Common Prayer, as the alternative canticle to the Te Deum.
feasts.source: Church of England, The Order for Morning Prayer (BCP).

pictures.text: Band, the owner's choice (Michelangelo's Daniel, daniel-band.jpg, is retired): Daniel in the Lions' Den, Briton Rivière, 1872, Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool (WAG 2700). The Commons file is a 'warmed image': its uploader made it warmer and more saturated than the painting; the credit says so. Licence 'Public domain' read on the file page. 1600 x 1006, saved at its own size, q85. Daniel is seen from behind at about 81% across: posM 88% 50%, posD 85% 50%.

Portrait, the owner's choice (the Kirillo-Belozersky icon, daniel-2.jpg, is retired): Daniel Interpreting to Belshazzar the Writing on the Wall, Benjamin West, 1775, oil on canvas, Saint Louis Art Museum 485:2018. The museum marks it Public Domain and offers the 5676 x 3934 download; resized to 1500 x 1040, q85.
pictures.source: Saint Louis Art Museum object page (rights: Public Domain).

pictures.text: Gallery 1 and card, the owner's choice (the Strobel detail, daniel-3.jpg, and the icon card, daniel-card.jpg, are retired): The Prophet Daniel (the writing on the wall), Julius Schnorr von Carolsfeld, 1860. Licence 'Public domain' read on the file page. 1184 x 1013, the original file used as it is. Card: box (464, 1)-(732, 336), saved at its own 268 x 335 (the face sits near the top of a small file, so a 480 x 600 card would have to be enlarged).

Gallery 2, the owner's choice of a better copy (the old detail, daniel-4.jpg, is retired): Daniel in the Lions' Den, Peter Paul Rubens, about 1614 to 1616 (the museum's date; the Commons file says 1613 to 1615), National Gallery of Art, Washington. Licence 'Public domain' read on the file page. The whole painting, from the 3840 px thumbnail (original 4000 x 2709), resized to 1200 x 813, q85.

could_not_verify: Britannica online (Book of Daniel) returned error pages; the modern dating rests on the 1908 Catholic Encyclopedia and the 1911 Britannica.
Julius Africanus's own letter to Origen was not fetched; his objection is given as Origen's reply reports it.
The present Roman Martyrology (2004) was not fetched; the page rests on the 1916 edition.

A claim that Hippolytus's commentary on Daniel is the oldest surviving Christian commentary was not found in the Catholic Encyclopedia (it says only 'the fullest extant commentary on the Book of Daniel'): left out.
The Lives of the Prophets (burial in the royal tomb at Babylon) was not fetched; the tradition is given from the 1911 Britannica.
The Greek synaxarion's birthplace for Daniel (Upper Beth-horon, from Epiphanius) was read but not used.

checker_2026_09_25.checked: One light pass. Read the page whole. Checked against the texts on disk: the Catholic Encyclopedia 'Daniel' (about fourteen, 605 BC, 'Bel protect his life', the eunuch tradition 'accepted by many Fathers', 'now at least eighty years of age', the king sending him away before the furnace, the return to Judea); the 1916 Martyrology ('At Babylon, the holy prophet Daniel', 21 July); the LSB calendar (17 December, 'Daniel the Prophet and the Three Young Men'); the Coptic 23 Baramhat and its Gregorian date; the OCA ('survived into old age, but died in captivity'); Ambrose, Duties 1.35 (the meal in the den, footnoted to Bel); the 1911 Britannica's burial traditions (royal vault, the rabbis' Jerusalem) as the facts file records them; no Anglican day in the Church of England or Episcopal calendars. Capitals for God, italics, the Old Testament rule (no 'St Daniel'), the number tiles (none reads as a slight), every Commons licence (one API call: all four match the page) and the hub card (face centred, eyes about 40% down).
changed: The feasts note said churches on the old calendar keep 'each date' 13 days later, which a reader could apply to the Coptic 1 April (already a Gregorian date). It now says they keep 17 December 13 days later.
left_for_owner: The troparion is our own translation from the Russian (verify-quotes kind 'own'); it reads close to the OCA's English, as any faithful translation would.
The eunuch tradition stays as one Family fact in the Catholic Encyclopedia's framing (the writer's call; it can come off).
